units: <cite ref="Berakhot 33b:3">Ber. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>הַוַּ׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) Thou, the known one!—
<cite ref="Mishnah Arakhin 1:1">Arakh. I, 1</cite> <he>זכר ו׳</he> a person distinctly male, <he>נקבה ודאית</he> distinctly female (no hermaphrodite &c.).
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 8:8">Yoma VIII, 8</cite>, a. fr. <he>אשם ו׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A03323"><he>אָשָׁם</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 2:7">Sabb. II, 7</cite> <he>הו׳</he> that which undoubtedly requires the separation of the tithes, opp. <cite ref="D00871"><he>דְּמַאי</he></cite>.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 1:3:4">Y. Bets. I, 60ᵇ</cite> <he>וַודָּייוֹ</he>, <cite ref="F00014"><he>וַודָּיָיהּ</he></cite> where there is no doubt about it, opp. <he>ספיקו</he>, <cite ref="O01366"><he>ספיקה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kiddushin 4:3">Kidd. IV, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Kiddushin 74a">74ᵃ</cite>) <cite ref="F00013"><he>וַדָּאָן</he></cite> the sure cases among them.—

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 2:25">Num. R. s. 2</cite>, end <he>אכילה וודייה</he> Ar. ed. Koh. (ed. <he>ידאית</he>) the eating (in <cite ref="Exodus 24:11">Ex. XXIV, 11</cite>) was a real one (physical refreshment, no metaphor); a. v. fr.

Ex. R. s. 3 לכה וודאית וכ׳ (strike out the gloss הה״א בסוף וכ׳) the word l’khah (Ex. III, 3) is emphatic (as if = לְךָ unto thee it belongs), if not thou &c.; Y. Succ. IV, 54ᶜ top לך יודייה (read: לכה וו׳) the l’khah (Ps. LXXX, 3) has the emphatic form (unto thee as well as unto us).—3) (noun) certainty, undisputed fact.—אין ספק מוציא מידי ו׳ doubt cannot take a case out of the status of certainty.

Ab. Zar. 41ᵇ הוי ספק וּוַ׳ ואין וכ׳ here is a doubt (the idolatrous character of an object may have been given up) against a certainty (that it was an idol) and the doubt cannot set aside the certainty.
Pes. 9ᵃ; a. fr.—בְּוַ׳, וַ׳ (adv.) surely, indeed; in reality. Y. Keth. V, 29ᵈ.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 98:4">Gen. R. s. 98</cite> <he>עלית בו׳</he> ‘thou didst ascend’ thy father’s couch (<cite ref="Genesis 49:4">Gen. XLIX, 4</cite>) means in reality (no metaphor).

<cite ref="Genesis 49:4">Ib.</cite> <he>חללת ו׳</he> ‘thou didst defile’ (<cite ref="Genesis 49:4">ib.</cite>) is to be taken literally. Pes. l. c. <he>דו׳ מעשרי</he> for it is sure that they separate the tithes.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 55:6">Gen. R. s. 55</cite> <he>נסה אותו בו׳</he> He tried him in the true sense of the word (gave him time); a. e.
